title: With an idempotency key, the retry gets the stored response, not a second charge
caption: The client picks the key once per checkout and resends it on every attempt; the server claims it before doing the work.

messages.label: POST /pay $30 · Key: 7f3a
messages.note: The client generates the UUID 7f3a when the user presses Pay, not per attempt.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a (in_progress)
messages.note: The unique key column makes this claim succeed exactly once.

messages.label: charge $30 · key 7f3a
messages.note: The key is passed downstream too, so the processor also dedupes.

messages.label: UPDATE 7f3a: done, 201 {pay_42}
messages.note: The response is stored next to the key.

messages.label: 201 {pay_42} (lost)
messages.note: Same failure as before: the reply never arrives.

messages.label: POST /pay $30 · Key: 7f3a (retry)
messages.note: Same key, same body.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a → conflict, row is done
messages.note: The claim fails, and the existing row says the work is finished.

messages.label: 201 {pay_42} (replayed)
messages.note: Byte-for-byte the original response. One charge, and the client can't tell it was a retry.

scenarios.name: Retry while in progress
scenarios.summary: The retry lands while the first attempt is still charging: the claim hits an in_progress row, so the API answers 409 instead of charging twice.

messages.label: POST /pay $30 · Key: 7f3a
messages.note: First attempt.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a (in_progress)
messages.note: The claim wins.

messages.label: charge $30 · key 7f3a
messages.note: The card network is slow today: 8 seconds.

messages.label: POST /pay $30 · Key: 7f3a (retry)
messages.note: The client's 5 s timeout fires and it retries while attempt 1 is still running.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a → conflict, in_progress
messages.note: Same key and body hash, but no response is stored yet: there is nothing to replay.

messages.label: 409 Conflict · retry later
messages.note: Don't charge and don't hold the connection open: tell the client to back off. Its next retry, after attempt 1 stores 201 {pay_42}, gets the replay.

scenarios.name: Same key, new body
scenarios.summary: Key 7f3a is reused for a $45 payment: the stored body hash doesn't match, so the API refuses with 422 instead of replaying the $30 answer.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a + hash($30) → done
messages.note: Claimed, charged and stored with the request fingerprint.

messages.label: POST /pay $45 · Key: 7f3a
messages.note: A client bug: the key was cached across two checkouts.

messages.label: INSERT 7f3a → conflict, hash differs
messages.note: Same key, different fingerprint.

messages.label: 422 key reused
messages.note: Replaying pay_42 would tell the client its $45 payment succeeded. Refuse loudly so the bug gets fixed.

scenarios.name: Risk: TTL too short
scenarios.summary: Keys expire after 1 hour but the app retries the next morning: the key is gone, so the retry charges again. The TTL must outlive the longest retry horizon.

messages.label: charge $30 · key 7f3a
messages.note: Claimed and charged; the key row is stored with a 1-hour TTL.

messages.label: 201 {pay_42} (lost)
messages.note: The reply is lost and the phone goes offline with the retry queued.

messages.label: TTL expired: delete 7f3a
messages.note: An hour later the clean-up job removes the key.

messages.label: POST /pay $30 · Key: 7f3a (next day)
messages.note: Same key, same body, but the server no longer remembers it.

messages.label: charge $30 again
messages.note: The claim succeeds on an empty slot: a second charge. Keep keys for longer than any client may retry (a day or more), and have clients give up on retries older than that.
